data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Console_Region.Help
data.value: Determines which region/hardware to emulate. Auto-Detect will use the region of the disc inserted.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_BIOS_PatchFastBoot.Help
data.value: Skips the BIOS shell/intro, booting directly into the game. Usually safe to enable, but some games break.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_RegionCheck.Help
data.value: Prevents discs from incorrect regions being read by the emulator. Usually safe to disable.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_ReadThread.Help
data.value: Reads CD-ROM sectors ahead asynchronously, reducing the risk of frame time spikes.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_LoadImagePatches.Help
data.value: Automatically applies patches to disc images when they are present in the same directory. Currently only PPF patches are supported with this option. Requires the core to be restarted to apply.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_LoadImageToRAM.Help
data.value: Loads the disc image to RAM before starting emulation. May reduce hitching if you are running off a network share, at a cost of a greater startup time. As libretro provides no way to draw overlays, the emulator will appear to lock up while the image is preloaded.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_PreCacheCHD.Help
data.value: Pre-caches CHD CD-ROM images to RAM without decompressing them. Unlike the preload option, this option supports M3U files. It is also faster and requires less RAM compared to preloading as it doesn't decompress the CHD.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_MuteCDAudio.Help
data.value: Forcibly mutes both CD-DA and XA audio from the CD-ROM. Can be used to disable background music in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_ReadSpeedup.Help
data.value: Speeds up CD-ROM reads by the specified factor. Only applies to double-speed reads, and is ignored when audio is playing. May improve loading speeds in some games, at the cost of breaking others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_SeekSpeedup.Help
data.value: Speeds up CD-ROM seeks by the specified factor. May improve loading speeds in some game, at the cost of breaking others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CPU_ExecutionMode.Help
data.value: Which mode to use for CPU emulation. Recompiler provides the best performance.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_Renderer.Help
data.value: Which renderer to use to emulate the GPU.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_ResolutionScale.Help
data.value: Scales internal VRAM resolution by the specified multiplier for the hardware renderer. Larger values are slower. Some games require 1x VRAM resolution or they will have rendering issues.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_UseThread.Help
data.value: Uses a second thread for drawing graphics. Currently only available for the software renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_UseSoftwareRendererForReadbacks.Help
data.value: Run software rendering alongside hardware rendering when reading image data from VRAM. Some games need this for motion blur or battle transitions, or to fix damaged textures. Restart the core after changing this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_MSAA.Help
data.value: Uses multisample antialiasing for rendering 3D objects. Can smooth out jagged edges on polygons at a lower cost to performance compared to increasing the resolution scale, but may be more likely to cause rendering errors in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_TrueColor.Help
data.value: Disables dithering and uses the full 8 bits per channel of color information. May break rendering in some games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_ScaledDithering.Help
data.value: Scales the dithering pattern with the internal rendering resolution, making it less noticeable. Usually safe to enable.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_DisableInterlacing.Help
data.value: Disables interlaced rendering and display in the GPU. Some games can render in 480p this way, but others will break.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_ForceNTSCTimings.Help
data.value: Forces PAL games to run at NTSC timings, i.e. 60hz. Some PAL games will run at their "normal" speeds, while others will break.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_Force4_3For24Bit.Help
data.value: Switches back to 4:3 display aspect ratio when displaying 24-bit content, usually FMVs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_ChromaSmoothing24Bit.Help
data.value: Smooths out blockyness between colour transitions in 24-bit content, usually FMVs. Only applies to the hardware renderers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_TextureFilter.Help
data.value: Smooths out the blockyness of magnified textures on 3D object by using bilinear filtering. Will have a greater effect on higher resolution scales. Only applies to the hardware renderers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_WidescreenHack.Help
data.value: Increases the field of view from 4:3 to the chosen display aspect ratio in 3D games. For 2D games, or games which use pre-rendered backgrounds, this enhancement will not work as expected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPEnable.Help
data.value: Reduces "wobbly" polygons by attempting to preserve the fractional component through memory transfers. Only works with the hardware renderers, and may not be compatible with all games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPCulling.Help
data.value: Increases the precision of polygon culling, reducing the number of holes in geometry. Requires geometry correction enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPTextureCorrection.Help
data.value: Uses perspective-correct interpolation for texture coordinates, straightening out warped textures. Requires geometry correction enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPColorCorrection.Help
data.value: Correct the interpolation of vertex colors according to perspective. This can improve the appearance of some games, but can cause graphics errors in others. Geometry correction must be enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPDepthBuffer.Help
data.value: Attempts to reduce polygon Z-fighting by testing pixels against the depth values from PGXP. Low compatibility, but can work well in some games. Requires geometry correction enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPVertexCache.Help
data.value: Uses screen coordinates as a fallback when tracking vertices through memory fails. May improve PGXP compatibility.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPCPU.Help
data.value: Tries to track vertex manipulation through the CPU. Some games require this option for PGXP to be effective. Very slow, and incompatible with the recompiler.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPPreserveProjFP.Help
data.value: Enables additional precision for PGXP. May improve visuals in some games but break others.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPTolerance.Help
data.value: Ignores precise positions if the difference exceeds this threshold.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_PGXPDepthClearThreshold.Help
data.value: Sets the threshold for the PGXP Depth Buffer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_AspectRatio.Help
data.value: Sets the preferred aspect ratio. Will only work when the 'Core Provided' aspect ratio is selected inside RetroArch's Video settings. Will be forced to 'Corrected (NTSC)' when using a Namco GunCon controller

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_CustomAspectRatioNumerator.Help
data.value: Sets the numerator for the custom aspect ratio, e.g. 4 in 4:3.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_CustomAspectRatioDenominator.Help
data.value: Sets the denominator for the custom aspect ratio, e.g. 3 in 4:3.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_CropMode.Help
data.value: Changes how much of the image is cropped. Some games display garbage in the overscan area which is typically hidden.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_DownsampleMode.Help
data.value: Downsamples the rendered image prior to displaying it. Can improve overall image quality in mixed 2D/3D games, but should be disabled for pure 3D games. Only applies to the hardware renderers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Value.BoxDownsample3DSmoothAll
data.value: Average nearby pixels to reduce 3D resolution and smooth the whole image

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_GPU_ShaderPrecompile.Help
data.value: Choose when to compile fragment shaders for hardware rendering. Deferred compilation is the default. It runs on a background thread while the game starts immediately. The enabled mode retains the previous behavior: the application waits for compilation before starting. Disabling advance compilation instead compiles each shader on the main thread when the game first uses it. This starts the game sooner, but new shader combinations may cause brief pauses during early gameplay. Changing the texture filter compiles all combinations again and incurs the same cost.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Value.EnabledBlockUntilDoneLikeOldBehaviour
data.value: Enabled (block until done, like old behaviour)

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_ShowOSDMessages.Help
data.value: Shows on-screen messages generated by the core.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_ActiveStartOffset.Help
data.value: Pads or crops off lines from the left of the displayed image.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_ActiveEndOffset.Help
data.value: Pads or crops off lines from the right of the displayed image.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_LineStartOffset.Label
data.value: Offset of the first displayed line

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_LineStartOffset.Help
data.value: Pads or crops off lines from the top of the displayed image.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_LineEndOffset.Label
data.value: Offset of the last displayed line

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Display_LineEndOffset.Help
data.value: Pads or crops off lines from the bottom of the displayed image.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_MemoryCards_Card1Type.Help
data.value: Choose the memory card format for slot 1. Restart the core when changing formats. Shared cards and the two separate-card options are retained for old configurations, but are not supported. The Libretro format uses .srm files. A separate card named after the game uses .mcd files. These two formats contain identical data. To convert between them, change the file extension and add or remove the slot suffix _1.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_MemoryCards_Card2Type.Help
data.value: Sets the type of memory card for Slot 2.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_MemoryCards_UsePlaylistTitle.Help
data.value: When using a playlist (m3u) and per-game (title) memory cards, a single memory card will be used for all discs. If unchecked, a separate card will be used for each disc.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_ControllerPorts_MultitapMode.Help
data.value: Sets the mode for the multitap.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller_AnalogCombo.Help
data.value: Sets the combo used to toggle analog mode.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Value.L1PlusL2PlusR1PlusR2PlusStartPlusSelect
data.value: L1 + L2 + R1 + R2 + Start + Select

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller_EnableRumble.Help
data.value: Enable haptic feedback when using a rumble-equipped gamepad with a supported input device.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller_ShowCrosshair.Label
data.value: Show the aiming cursor for GunCon

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller_ShowCrosshair.Help
data.value: Show a crosshair when the input device is set to 'Namco GunCon'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_ForceAnalog.Help
data.value: Forces analog mode to be always on. May cause issues with some games. Only use this option for games that support analog mode but do not automatically enable it themselves. When disabled, analog mode can be toggled by pressing and holding the DualShock Analog Mode Combo.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_AnalogDPadInDigitalMode.Label

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_AnalogDPadInDigitalMode.Help
data.value: Allows you to use the analog sticks to control the d-pad in digital mode, as well as the buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_AxisScale.Help
data.value: Sets the analog stick axis scaling factor.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_VibrationBias.Help
data.value: Applies an offset to vibration intensities, higher values will make smaller vibrations more noticable.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_XScale.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_YScale.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_SteeringDeadzone.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Controller1_TwistResponse.Help

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CDROM_ReadaheadSectors.Help
data.value: Determines how far the CD-ROM thread will read ahead. Can reduce hitches on slow storage mediums or with compressed games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CPU_Overclock.Help
data.value: Runs the emulated CPU faster or slower than native speed, which can improve framerates in some games. Will break other games and increase system requirements, use with caution.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Main_ApplyGameSettings.Help
data.value: Automatically disables enhancements on games which are incompatible.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Logging_LogLevel.Help
data.value: Sets the level of information logged by the core.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CPU_RecompilerICache.Help
data.value: Determines whether the CPU's instruction cache is simulated in the recompiler. Improves accuracy at a small cost to performance. If games are running too fast, try enabling this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CPU_RecompilerBlockLinking.Help
data.value: Enables the generated code to directly jump between blocks without going through the dispatcher. Provides a measurable speed boost.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CPU_FastmemMode.Help
data.value: Uses page faults to determine hardware memory accesses at runtime. Can provide a significant performance improvement in some games, but make the core more difficult to debug.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CPU_FastmemRewrite.Label
data.value: CPU Recompiler Fast Memory Access Rewrite

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_CPU_FastmemRewrite.Help
data.value: Rewrite instructions when fast memory access is enabled for the CPU recompiler. This can improve speed. It can also cause the emulator to crash on some platforms.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_TextureReplacements_EnableVRAMWriteReplacements.Help
data.value: Replace 'VRAM write textures' with DuckStation-formatted texture packs from the 'swanstation/textures' folder inside the frontend's system directory. This only works with the Vulkan and D3D11 (where available) renderers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_TextureReplacements_PreloadTextures.Help
data.value: Preload VRAM write replacement textures to RAM

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Main_RunaheadFrameCount.Help
data.value: Simulates the system ahead of time and rolls back/replays to reduce input lag. Has very high system requirements. Most libretro frontends (including RetroArch) provide their own run-ahead implementation in their settings; the frontend version is generally more efficient and supports both single- and second-instance modes, so prefer it when available and leave this option at 0. Only enable this internal version if the frontend does not offer its own run-ahead, or to test against it.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Console_Enable8MBRAM.Help
data.value: Enabled an additional 6MB of RAM, usually present on dev consoles. Games have to use a larger heap size for this additional RAM to be usable, and may break games which rely on memory mirroring, so it should only be used with compatible mods.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Hacks_OldMDECRoutines.Help
data.value: Use old routines for MDEC content. The newer routines may look better with some games, worse with others. As VRAM write texture replacements require either the old or new routines to function, it's adviced to toggle this setting to the routines required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.swanstation.swanstation_Audio_FastHook.Help
data.value: Drains all SPU samples to the frontend once per emulated frame, instead of pushing each chunk as the SPU produces it. This is faster and produces more even audio batching, and is the right choice for almost every game. A small number of titles (notably Formula 1 / Formula 1 '97) hang at boot if audio is not delivered to the frontend mid-frame; the core auto-disables this option for those known titles, but if a game freezes at startup with audio enabled, try disabling this manually.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_cpu_freq_scale.Help
data.value: Overclock (or underclock) the emulated PSX CPU. Overclocking can eliminate slowdown and improve frame rates in certain games at the expense of increased performance requirements. Note that some games have an internal frame rate limiter and may not benefit from overclocking. May cause certain effects to animate faster than intended in some titles when overclocked.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_gpu_overclock.Help
data.value: Increase the speed of the 2D drawing unit inside the emulated PSX GPU. This does not improve 3D graphics and usually has little effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_gte_overclock.Help
data.value: Execute every operation of the GTE graphics coprocessor in one CPU cycle. This can greatly improve the frame rate and make frame timing more stable in games that use the GTE heavily.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_cd_access_method.Help
data.value: Synchronous access reproduces the original hardware. Asynchronous access can reduce pauses on devices with slow storage. Loading the whole disc image into RAM can improve loading times during the game, but delays startup. This mode can cause problems when RAM is limited. Physical discs use synchronous access instead of loading the whole image. Restart after changing this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_cd_fastload.Help
data.value: Values higher than '2x (Native)' can greatly reduce in-game loading times, but may introduce timing errors. Some games may not function properly above a certain value.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_skip_bios.Help
data.value: Do not show the PlayStation BIOS animation when starting a game. This option can cause problems in some games, including games with PAL copy protection and Saga Frontier.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_override_bios.Help
data.value: Override the standard region specific BIOS with a region-free one if found. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_region.Help
data.value: Sets the fallback region used when content cannot be auto-detected (e.g. raw PS-X EXE files). Disc-based games still use the region embedded on the disc. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_internal_resolution.Help
data.value: Resolutions higher than '1x (Native)' improve fidelity of 3D models at the expense of increased performance requirements. 2D elements are generally unaffected by this setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dither_mode.Help
data.value: '1x (Native)' emulates native low resolution dithering used by original hardware to smooth out color banding artifacts visible at native color depth. 'Internal Resolution' scales dithering granularity to the configured internal resolution for cleaner results. Recommended to be disabled when running at 32 bpp color depth. Note: On Vulkan, enabling this will force downsampling to native color depth, while disabling will automatically enable output at higher color depth.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_pgxp_mode.Help
data.value: Render 3D objects with subpixel precision, minimizing distortion and jitter of 3D objects seen on original hardware due to the usage of fixed point vertex coordinates. 'Memory Only' mode has minimal compatibility issues and is recommended for general use. 'Memory + CPU (Buggy)' mode can reduce jitter even further but has high performance requirements and may cause various geometry errors.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_pgxp_2d_tol.Help
data.value: Reduce obvious errors from PGXP. Choose how much variation is allowed when retaining PGXP values for geometry without reliable depth information.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_pgxp_nclip.Help
data.value: Use PGXP's NCLIP implementation. Improves appearance by reducing holes in geometries with PGXP coordinates. Known to cause some games to lock up in various circumstances.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_pgxp_texture.Help
data.value: Replace native PSX affine texture mapping with perspective correct texture mapping. Eliminates position-dependent distortion and warping of textures, resulting in properly aligned textures. This option is applied only when PGXP Operation Mode is enabled. Supported by the hardware renderers and the software renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_display_internal_fps.Help
data.value: Display the internal frame rate at which the emulated PlayStation system is rendering content. Note: Requires onscreen notifications to be enabled in the libretro frontend.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_display_osd.Help
data.value: Display OSD messages generated by the core.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_analog_calibration.Help
data.value: Enable dynamic calibration of analog inputs when the device is set to DualShock, Analog Controller, Analog Joystick, or neGcon. Maximum registered input values are monitored in real time and used to scale analog coordinates passed to the emulator. This should be used for games such as Mega Man Legends 2 that expect larger values than what modern controllers provide. For best results, analog sticks should be rotated at full extent to tune the calibration algorithm each time content is loaded.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_analog_toggle.Help
data.value: When the input device type is DualShock, this option allows the emulated DualShock to be toggled between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode like original hardware. Mode can also be toggled by using the selected button combination.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_analog_toggle_combo.Help
data.value: The button combination that will be used to toggle between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode for the emulated DualShock.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_analog_toggle_hold.Label
data.value: DualShock Analog Mode Combo Hold Delay

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_analog_toggle_hold.Help
data.value: Hold time for the analog mode combo buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_gun_input_mode.Help
data.value: Use mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input when device type is set to 'Guncon/G-Con 45' or 'Justifier'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_gun_cursor.Help
data.value: Draw a cursor on screen while using the 'Guncon/G-Con 45' and 'Justifier' input device types.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_crosshair_color_p1.Help
data.value: Light gun crosshair color for port 1.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_crosshair_color_p2.Help
data.value: Light gun crosshair color for port 2.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_mouse_sensitivity.Help
data.value: Responsiveness of the 'Mouse' input device type.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_negcon_response.Help
data.value: Left analog stick response type when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated 'neGcon' input devices. Analog stick displacement may be mapped to neGcon rotation angle either linearly, quadratically or cubically. 'Quadratic' allows for greater precision than 'Linear' when making small movements. 'Cubic' further increases small movement precision, but 'exaggerates' larger movements. Note: 'Linear' is only recommended when using racing wheel peripherals. Conventional controllers implement analog input in a manner fundamentally different from the neGcon 'twist' mechanism, such that linear mapping over-amplifies small movements, impairing fine control. In most cases, 'Quadratic' provides the closest approximation of real hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_negcon_deadzone.Help
data.value: Left analog stick deadzone when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated 'neGcon' input devices. Used to eliminate controller drift. Note: Most neGcon-compatible titles provide in-game options for setting a 'twist' deadzone value. To avoid loss of precision, the in-game deadzone should *always* be set to zero. Any required adjustments should *only* be applied via this core option. This is particularly important when 'neGcon Twist Response' is set to 'Quadratic' or 'Cubic'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_use_mednafen_memcard0_method.Help
data.value: Save data format used for the left memory card slot. 'Mednafen' may be used for compatibility with the stand-alone version of Mednafen. When used with Beetle PSX, Libretro (.srm) and Mednafen (.mcr) saves have internally identical formats and can be converted between one another via renaming. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_enable_memcard1.Help
data.value: Emulate a second memory card in the right memory card slot. Note: Some games require this option to be disabled for correct operation (e.g. Codename Tenka). Note: Memory Card Slot 2 uses the Mednafen (.mcr) save format. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_shared_memory_cards.Help
data.value: Use shared memory cards instead of separate cards for each content. Note: if 'Memory Card Method' is set to 'Libretro', only memory card slot 2 will be affected. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_memcard_left_index.Help
data.value: Memory card currently loaded in the left slot. This option will only work if Memory Card Method is set to Mednafen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_memcard_right_index.Help
data.value: Memory card currently loaded in the right slot. This option will only work if Memory Card Slot 2 is enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_line_render.Help
data.value: Some games (e.g. Doom, Hexen, Soul Blade, etc.) draw horizontal lines by stretching single-pixel-high triangles across the screen, which are rasterized as a row of pixels on original hardware. This hack detects these small triangles and converts them to quads as required, allowing them to be displayed properly on the hardware renderers and at upscaled internal resolutions. 'Aggressive' is required for some titles (e.g. Dark Forces, Duke Nukem) but may otherwise introduce graphical glitches. Leave at 'Default' if unsure.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_widescreen_hack.Label
data.value: Modify the game for a wider screen

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_widescreen_hack.Help
data.value: Render 3D content anamorphically and output the emulated framebuffer at a widescreen aspect ratio. Produces best results with fully 3D games. 2D elements will be horizontally stretched and may be misaligned.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_widescreen_hack_aspect_ratio.Label
data.value: Aspect ratio for the wider screen

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_widescreen_hack_aspect_ratio.Help
data.value: Choose the aspect ratio used when modifying the game for a wider screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_spu_silent_voice.Help
data.value: Skip the per-sample processing of voices whose envelope has fully released. Audio output is identical; the optimization automatically disables itself while the SPU IRQ is in use. Saves roughly 5-10% of frame time. Disable for fully accurate SPU register state.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_cpu_dynarec.Help
data.value: Dynamically recompile CPU instructions to native instructions. Much faster than interpreter, but CPU timing is less accurate, and may have bugs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dynarec_invalidate.Help
data.value: Some games require 'Full' invalidation, some require 'DMA Only'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dynarec_op_cycles.Help
data.value: Cycles the dynarec charges per CPU instruction. '2' is faster, but the emulated CPU appears half-speed to games that pace themselves against it - set '1' for games whose CD streaming stalls or hangs under the dynarec (e.g. Parasite Eve 2). The '1' setting charges memory accesses two cycles and everything else one, close to the real CPU.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dynarec_eventcycles.Help
data.value: Max cycles run by CPU before a GPU/DMA/MDEC/Timer Update is checked, higher number will be faster, has much less impact on beetle interpreter than dynarec.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dynarec_spu_samples.Help
data.value: Max SPU samples to run before a SPU Update is checked, higher number will be faster, but will cause sound glitches in some games with anything other than 1.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dynarec_spgp_opt.Label
data.value: Dynarec SP GP Hit RAM Optimization

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_dynarec_spgp_opt.Help
data.value: Enabled will generate faster code, but potentially crash, by assuming sp and gp registers always point to ram, disabled is more widely compatible

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_compatibility_settings.Help
data.value: Apply compatibility settings per game and per setting. Disable to allow user-selected settings to override them.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_core_timing_fps.Help
data.value: Automatic Toggling allows the core to switch between progressive and interlaced rates.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Value.ForceProgressiveRate
data.value: Force the frame rate for progressive video

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Value.ForceInterlacedRate
data.value: Use the frame rate for video made of alternating odd and even lines

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_deinterlacer.Help
data.value: Weave joins both video fields in one frame. Still images retain full resolution. Bob reduces vertical resolution to make movement clearer. Bob (Offset) doubles the current field to fill the full image height. It shifts alternate fields by one line. This preserves the output resolution and smooth movement. FastMAD joins fields for still pixels and interpolates moving pixels vertically. It keeps full image height without comb-shaped artifacts during movement or the reduced resolution of Bob. When deinterlacing is disabled, the software renderer behaves like the Vulkan and OpenGL renderers. Every frame draws all VRAM lines before displaying the image. This removes comb-shaped artifacts in interlaced games. Some programs transfer data to VRAM while the image is being displayed. Some PAL demos do this with image buffers taller than 512 lines that wrap around. Other games, such as Pro Pinball, update moving sprites through CPU transfers to VRAM timed to the displayed field. These programs may show old image rows or duplicate sprite images when deinterlacing is disabled. Use Weave, Bob, Bob (Offset) or FastMAD for these programs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_frame_duping.Help
data.value: Repeat the previous frame if the core has nothing new to display.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_pal_video_timing_override.Label
data.value: Override the timing of PAL video

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_pal_video_timing_override.Help
data.value: Due to different standards, PAL games often appear slowed down compared to the American or Japanese NTSC releases. This option can be used to override PAL timings in order to attempt to run these games with the NTSC framerate.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_aspect_ratio.Help
data.value: This setting is ignored when the Widescreen Mode Hack or Display Full VRAM options are enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_crop_overscan.Help
data.value: Full native image or no borders.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_image_crop.Help
data.value: Reduce the width of the cropped image by the specified number of pixels.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_image_offset.Help
data.value: Offset horizontally to the right (positive) or left (negative) by the specified number of pixels. May be used to correct alignment issues. Only supported by the software renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_initial_scanline.Help
data.value: First displayed scan line when running NTSC content. Values greater than zero will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the topmost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_last_scanline.Help
data.value: Last displayed scan line when running NTSC content. Values less than 239 will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the bottommost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_initial_scanline_pal.Help
data.value: First displayed scan line when running PAL content. Values greater than zero will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the topmost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx.beetle_psx_last_scanline_pal.Help
data.value: Last displayed scan line when running PAL content. Values below 287 will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the bottommost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_cpu_freq_scale.Help
data.value: Overclock (or underclock) the emulated PSX CPU. Overclocking can eliminate slowdown and improve frame rates in certain games at the expense of increased performance requirements. Note that some games have an internal frame rate limiter and may not benefit from overclocking. May cause certain effects to animate faster than intended in some titles when overclocked.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_gpu_overclock.Help
data.value: Increase the speed of the 2D drawing unit inside the emulated PSX GPU. This does not improve 3D graphics and usually has little effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_gte_overclock.Help
data.value: Execute every operation of the GTE graphics coprocessor in one CPU cycle. This can greatly improve the frame rate and make frame timing more stable in games that use the GTE heavily.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_cd_access_method.Help
data.value: Synchronous access reproduces the original hardware. Asynchronous access can reduce pauses on devices with slow storage. Loading the whole disc image into RAM can improve loading times during the game, but delays startup. This mode can cause problems when RAM is limited. Physical discs use synchronous access instead of loading the whole image. Restart after changing this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_cd_fastload.Help
data.value: Values higher than '2x (Native)' can greatly reduce in-game loading times, but may introduce timing errors. Some games may not function properly above a certain value.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_skip_bios.Help
data.value: Do not show the PlayStation BIOS animation when starting a game. This option can cause problems in some games, including games with PAL copy protection and Saga Frontier.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_override_bios.Help
data.value: Override the standard region specific BIOS with a region-free one if found. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_region.Help
data.value: Sets the fallback region used when content cannot be auto-detected (e.g. raw PS-X EXE files). Disc-based games still use the region embedded on the disc. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_internal_resolution.Help
data.value: Resolutions higher than '1x (Native)' improve fidelity of 3D models at the expense of increased performance requirements. 2D elements are generally unaffected by this setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_renderer.Help
data.value: Choose how to draw the image. The software renderer is the most accurate. It needs much more processing power at higher internal resolutions. Hardware rendering is less accurate, but faster at higher resolutions and supports graphics improvements. Automatic hardware rendering chooses Vulkan or OpenGL according to the video driver used by the application. If the driver supports neither Vulkan nor OpenGL 3.3, the core uses software rendering instead. Restart the core after changing this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_renderer_software_fb.Help
data.value: Use the software renderer in the background at the native resolution while the hardware renderer displays the game. This reproduces motion blur and battle transitions in FF7 accurately. When disabled, OpenGL omits these effects and Vulkan draws them on the GPU. Disabling this option can improve speed but can also cause serious graphics errors. Keep it enabled if unsure.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_color_format.Help
data.value: Selects the output color depth. '24-bit (Standard)' is the historical 8-bit-per-channel output. '30-bit Color (HDR)' outputs 10-bit-per-channel, PQ-encoded Rec.2020 (HDR10) for display on an HDR-capable screen: the renderer already carries more than 8 bits of internal precision, so this both reduces banding on upscaled gradients and lets emissive content sit above SDR white. Takes effect with the Vulkan and OpenGL hardware renderers and requires frontend HDR support; it falls back to 24-bit on the Software renderer or when the frontend cannot present HDR10. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hdr_shoulder.Help
data.value: Choose how to compress bright additive effects above SDR white toward the HDR peak in 30-bit hardware rendering. Reinhard compresses brightness gradually with a soft transition. ACES increases faster and reaches the peak sooner, making bright effects stronger. This affects only emitted or additive light above reference white. Ordinary colors and values in the standard range remain identical. This option has no effect on software rendering or 24-bit output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_src_primaries.Help
data.value: Selects the chromaticities the game's colours are interpreted against. PSX content was not authored on a modern Rec.709 display, and which real colours a given RGB value stands for depends on the monitor it was made on. This is independent of 'Analog Video Cable' - primaries belong to the authoring display, not the wire - so it applies to RGB output as well. 'Rec.709' (default) leaves the picture matching the 24-bit path. 'SMPTE-C' is the NTSC-era studio standard and shifts colour by around 6%. 'EBU' is the PAL equivalent and differs from Rec.709 in green alone, by about 4%. 'NTSC 1953' is the original FCC standard, dramatically wider - its green sits 40% outside Rec.709 and is only representable at all on a wide-gamut HDR display. 'Auto' picks SMPTE-C or EBU from the disc region. Works in 24-bit mode too, though every option maps some colours outside Rec.709 and a standard display clips those - 'NTSC 1953' in particular only shows properly on a wide-gamut HDR screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_black_setup.Help
data.value: Simulates a mismatch in where black sits in the signal. NTSC-M, as used in North America, places black 7.5 IRE above blanking; NTSC-J in Japan and PAL everywhere else place it at 0. A console and television from the same market cancel out and look correct, so this does nothing by default - it only matters when a disc crossed between them, which is the better documented difference between NTSC-J and NTSC-M hardware. 'Lifted' reads a North American signal without the compensation, raising black to about 7.5% so the picture looks washed out. 'Crushed' reads a Japanese signal as though it carried the pedestal, clipping everything below 7.5% to black and raising contrast. Only affects 'Analog Video Cable' modes other than RGB, which carries no pedestal, and has no effect on PAL discs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_phase_error.Help
data.value: Misaligns the decoder's colour carrier by the given number of degrees, as a mistuned or drifting television would be. Zero on a direct cable; a real effect over RF, where the modulator and channel introduce it. The two systems fail very differently, which is the point: on NTSC the whole picture shifts hue and stays shifted, while on PAL the error lands opposite on alternate lines and the decoder's delay line averages most of it back out, trading a little saturation for it. Only affects 'Analog Video Cable' modes other than RGB.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_video_cable.Help
data.value: Simulates the cable between the console and the television, including the colour encoding and the television's decoder. 'No Simulation' switches the chain off entirely and hands the framebuffer straight to the display (default). 'RGB (SCART)' is the sharpest output the PSX could produce: the multi-out carries analog RGB, so nothing is modulated and none of the encoding artifacts below can occur - but it is still an analog wire, so it is band-limited by the console's video amplifier and the set's input stage rather than being infinitely sharp. 'S-Video' band-limits colour heavily but keeps luma and colour on separate wires, so fine detail stays clean. 'Composite' sums them onto one wire, which the decoder then has to pull apart again, costing luma detail and adding colour smearing and rainbow fringing on fine patterns. 'RF' models an external modulator - the console itself has none, only a DC jack to power one - narrowing luma further and adding the beat pattern the sound carrier makes against the colour subcarrier, which is strongest on saturated colour. Works at any internal resolution: the extra samples are resolved down before the signal is generated, so higher settings act as supersampling into the cable rather than a wider signal, and the output still carries the sub-pixel detail the decoder produces. Supported by the Vulkan and OpenGL renderers, and ignored by the Software renderer. On OpenGL the filter that removes 'hanging dots' - the fine dotted pattern along horizontal colour edges - needs GL 4.3 or GLES 3.1; on an older driver the simulation still runs, but 'Composite' and 'RF' will show those dots. Applies immediately; no restart needed.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hdr_sdr_gamma.Help
data.value: Choose the gamma curve assumed for the screen that displays the console image. This curve converts image values to linear light before HDR encoding. It also determines how to average samples when reducing resolution or combining multiple samples. Samples are averaged as emitted light, rather than as stored numbers. The choice matches HDR brightness to the standard image on your screen; it does not change emulation accuracy. The default BT.1886 curve uses gamma 2.4. It matches the application conversion from SDR to HDR and a reference television. Gamma 2.2 suits a PC monitor with the usual sRGB response. The segmented sRGB curve matches the Windows presentation of standard content on an HDR desktop and reveals more detail in dark areas. Try gamma 2.2 or the segmented sRGB curve if HDR is darker or has more contrast than 24-bit output on the same screen. This option does not affect software rendering.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hdr_overbright.Help
data.value: Allow additive and subtractive effects to exceed reference white in 30-bit HDR hardware rendering. In OpenGL, this affects additive effects only. When disabled, each source is limited to reference white before blending, as on the original hardware. Highlights can exceed white only where transparent layers overlap. When enabled, bright modulated sources can make additive and subtractive effects roughly twice as strong. Lasers, lightning and flames can look brighter in a single layer, at the cost of accuracy. Opaque surfaces remain limited in both modes. This option has no effect on software rendering or 24-bit output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hdr_multipass.Help
data.value: Choose how to blend subtractive transparency in 30-bit HDR output with Vulkan. Both modes limit the result to zero, as on the original hardware. When disabled, the graphics hardware blends each batch and a simple extra pass limits negative results. This is accurate and almost free. When enabled, each subtractive drawing operation instead uses the programmable blending method also used for pixel mask tests. The option for brighter HDR effects can then strengthen subtractive effects as well. This can produce deeper dark areas in a single layer, but each operation requires synchronization. Many subtractive operations, such as shadows and screen fades, can increase this cost. This option has no effect on OpenGL, software rendering or 24-bit output.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_depth.Help
data.value: Higher color depth can reduce color banding effects without the use of dithering. 16 bpp emulates original hardware but may have visible banding if dithering is not enabled. 'Dithering Pattern' is recommended to be disabled when this option is set to 32 bpp.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dither_mode.Help
data.value: '1x (Native)' emulates native low resolution dithering used by original hardware to smooth out color banding artifacts visible at native color depth. 'Internal Resolution' scales dithering granularity to the configured internal resolution for cleaner results. Recommended to be disabled when running at 32 bpp color depth. Note: On Vulkan, enabling this will force downsampling to native color depth, while disabling will automatically enable output at higher color depth.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_native_color.Help
data.value: Vulkan renderer only. Stores every GPU write at the PlayStation's native 15-bit color depth inside the framebuffer, quantizing each draw at write time exactly as the original hardware does, instead of rendering at 24-bit and only reducing color depth for display. Fixes brightness seams and framebuffer-feedback artifacts in some games (e.g. Silent Hill's intro logos), at the cost of visible banding on upscaled gradients and texture filtering, and reduced batching of semi-transparent primitives. Has no effect when 'Color Format' is set to '30-bit Color (HDR)' and HDR output is active.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_scaled_uv_offset.Help
data.value: Sample textures for 3D polygons at an offset for higher than 1x internal resolution. Reduces texture seams but may cause unintended graphical glitches.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_filter.Help
data.value: 'Nearest' emulates original hardware. 'Bilinear' and '3-Point' are smoothing filters, which reduce pixelation via blurring. 'SABR', 'xBR', and 'JINC2' are upscaling filters that may improve texture fidelity/sharpness at the expense of increased performance requirements. Only supported by the hardware renderers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_filter_exclude_sprite.Help
data.value: Do not apply texture filtering to sprites. Prevents seams in various games with 2D sprite-rendered backgrounds. Use together with Adaptive Smoothing or another post-processing filter for best effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_filter_exclude_2d_polygon.Help
data.value: Do not apply texture filtering to 2D polygons. 2D polygons are detected with a heuristic and there may be glitches. Use together with Adaptive Smoothing or another post-processing filter for best effect.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_adaptive_smoothing.Help
data.value: Smooth out 2D artwork and UI elements without blurring 3D rendered objects. Only supported by the Vulkan renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_super_sampling.Label
data.value: Render at a higher resolution and reduce to the native resolution

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_super_sampling.Help
data.value: Downsample rendered content from upscaled internal resolution down to native resolution. Combining this with higher internal resolution multipliers allows for games to be displayed with anti-aliased 3D objects at native low resolution. Produces best results when applied to titles that mix 2D and 3D elements (e.g. 3D characters on pre-rendered backgrounds), and works well in conjunction with CRT shaders. Only supported by the Vulkan renderer. Note: 'Dithering Pattern' is recommended to be disabled when enabling this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_msaa.Help
data.value: MSAA improves the appearance of 3D objects. Only supported by the Vulkan renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_mdec_yuv.Help
data.value: Reduce block-shaped artifacts and jagged edges in video playback to improve image quality. Only the Vulkan renderer supports this option.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_track_textures.Help
data.value: Prerequisite for texture dumping and replacement. Will probably crash in most games.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hd_dump_mode.Help
data.value: Choose how to export textures. This feature is experimental. Exporting uploaded regions is the default and matches the original Beetle behavior. Each tracked upload is saved in <cd>-texture-dump/. Exporting complete texture pages saves whole VRAM pages in <cd>-texture-dump-pages/, which produces cleaner tiles. Exporting both saves both formats in separate folders during the same playthrough. Choose later which format to edit. Packs made from complete pages cannot replace packs made from uploaded regions: their hashes cover different areas.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Value.UploadRectMatchMaster
data.value: Use uploaded texture regions, matching the reference version

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_replace_textures.Help
data.value: Replace textures using HD versions from <cd>-texture-replacements/

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_texture_directory.Help
data.value: Choose where to store exported textures and replacement textures. The content folder keeps them next to the game image, as before. The system folder or save folder stores texture packs in the location configured for that folder in RetroArch. This provides one central location for all games. Configure these paths in the directory settings. Each game has separate subfolders named <name>-texture-dump and <name>-texture-replacements, so files from different games do not collide. Changing this option scans the new folder for replacement textures.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hd_replacement_mode.Help
data.value: Choose where to find replacement textures. This feature is experimental. The default matches each uploaded region with files from <cd>-texture-replacements/, as in the original Beetle behavior. The complete-page mode matches whole VRAM pages with files from <cd>-texture-replacements-pages/. The texture export mode does not affect this choice. Packs made from complete pages cannot replace packs made from uploaded regions.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hd_replacement_fallback.Help
data.value: On an HD texture miss in the active HD Replacement Mode, also check the OTHER mode's folder before falling back to native. Works both ways: an upload-rect pack can fill gaps from a page-aligned pack and vice-versa, without converting packs. Best with the Lazy caching method.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_reduce_palette_range.Help
data.value: Opt-in. When dumping/replacing HD textures, hash only the palette (CLUT) entries the texture actually uses instead of the whole CLUT. This makes a texture's hash ignore unused palette entries that games often leave as garbage or rewrite over time, so one replacement keeps matching across those variations - fewer dumps and far better match coverage (most useful for 8bpp textures). Filenames are unchanged in format and remain loadable; old full-palette packs still match with this enabled (the matcher falls back to the full-palette hash when no reduced file is present). Applies to both the upload-rect and page-aligned paths. Re-dump a game to benefit.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hd_caching_method.Help
data.value: Choose when to load HD replacement textures. Immediate loading fetches every palette variant when a texture is uploaded, matching the original Beetle behavior. Deferred loading fetches a texture and its palette in the background when first drawn. This uses fewer resources, but the original texture may appear briefly before its replacement is ready. Synchronous deferred loading also loads on first use, but waits until the texture is ready. It avoids temporary original textures, but may cause brief pauses when many new textures appear together. These methods use the VRAM and RAM caches and capacity limits below.

data.name: Emulation.Option.Sony.Value.LazySynchronousNoPopIn
data.value: Load textures on first use and wait until ready, avoiding temporary missing textures

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hd_cache_vram_budget.Help
data.value: Maximum VRAM used to keep uploaded HD replacement textures resident. Higher keeps more textures ready (smoother) but can exhaust VRAM on smaller GPUs and cause slowdown; lower it if you see stutter. Only used with Replace Textures.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_hd_cache_ram_budget.Help
data.value: Maximum system RAM used to keep decoded HD replacement textures, so they don't have to be re-read from disk. Only used with Replace Textures.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_pgxp_mode.Help
data.value: Render 3D objects with subpixel precision, minimizing distortion and jitter of 3D objects seen on original hardware due to the usage of fixed point vertex coordinates. 'Memory Only' mode has minimal compatibility issues and is recommended for general use. 'Memory + CPU (Buggy)' mode can reduce jitter even further but has high performance requirements and may cause various geometry errors.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_pgxp_2d_tol.Help
data.value: Reduce obvious errors from PGXP. Choose how much variation is allowed when retaining PGXP values for geometry without reliable depth information.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_pgxp_nclip.Help
data.value: Use PGXP's NCLIP implementation. Improves appearance by reducing holes in geometries with PGXP coordinates. Known to cause some games to lock up in various circumstances.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_pgxp_vertex.Help
data.value: Cache PGXP-enhanced vertex positions for re-use across polygon draws. Can potentially improve object alignment and reduce visible seams when rendering textures, but false positives when querying the cache may produce graphical glitches. It is currently recommended to leave this option disabled. This option is applied only when PGXP Operation Mode is enabled. Only supported by the hardware renderers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_pgxp_texture.Help
data.value: Replace native PSX affine texture mapping with perspective correct texture mapping. Eliminates position-dependent distortion and warping of textures, resulting in properly aligned textures. This option is applied only when PGXP Operation Mode is enabled. Supported by the hardware renderers and the software renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_display_internal_fps.Help
data.value: Display the internal frame rate at which the emulated PlayStation system is rendering content. Note: Requires onscreen notifications to be enabled in the libretro frontend.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_display_osd.Help
data.value: Display OSD messages generated by the core.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_display_vram.Help
data.value: Visualize the entire emulated console's VRAM. Only supported by the OpenGL and Vulkan hardware renderers. Note: This is for debugging purposes, and should normally be disabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_analog_calibration.Help
data.value: Enable dynamic calibration of analog inputs when the device is set to DualShock, Analog Controller, Analog Joystick, or neGcon. Maximum registered input values are monitored in real time and used to scale analog coordinates passed to the emulator. This should be used for games such as Mega Man Legends 2 that expect larger values than what modern controllers provide. For best results, analog sticks should be rotated at full extent to tune the calibration algorithm each time content is loaded.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_analog_toggle.Help
data.value: When the input device type is DualShock, this option allows the emulated DualShock to be toggled between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode like original hardware. Mode can also be toggled by using the selected button combination.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_analog_toggle_combo.Help
data.value: The button combination that will be used to toggle between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode for the emulated DualShock.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_analog_toggle_hold.Label
data.value: DualShock Analog Mode Combo Hold Delay

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_analog_toggle_hold.Help
data.value: Hold time for the analog mode combo buttons.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_gun_input_mode.Help
data.value: Use mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input when device type is set to 'Guncon/G-Con 45' or 'Justifier'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_gun_cursor.Help
data.value: Draw a cursor on screen while using the 'Guncon/G-Con 45' and 'Justifier' input device types.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_crosshair_color_p1.Help
data.value: Light gun crosshair color for port 1.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_crosshair_color_p2.Help
data.value: Light gun crosshair color for port 2.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_mouse_sensitivity.Help
data.value: Responsiveness of the 'Mouse' input device type.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_negcon_response.Help
data.value: Left analog stick response type when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated 'neGcon' input devices. Analog stick displacement may be mapped to neGcon rotation angle either linearly, quadratically or cubically. 'Quadratic' allows for greater precision than 'Linear' when making small movements. 'Cubic' further increases small movement precision, but 'exaggerates' larger movements. Note: 'Linear' is only recommended when using racing wheel peripherals. Conventional controllers implement analog input in a manner fundamentally different from the neGcon 'twist' mechanism, such that linear mapping over-amplifies small movements, impairing fine control. In most cases, 'Quadratic' provides the closest approximation of real hardware.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_negcon_deadzone.Help
data.value: Left analog stick deadzone when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated 'neGcon' input devices. Used to eliminate controller drift. Note: Most neGcon-compatible titles provide in-game options for setting a 'twist' deadzone value. To avoid loss of precision, the in-game deadzone should *always* be set to zero. Any required adjustments should *only* be applied via this core option. This is particularly important when 'neGcon Twist Response' is set to 'Quadratic' or 'Cubic'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_use_mednafen_memcard0_method.Help
data.value: Save data format used for the left memory card slot. 'Mednafen' may be used for compatibility with the stand-alone version of Mednafen. When used with Beetle PSX, Libretro (.srm) and Mednafen (.mcr) saves have internally identical formats and can be converted between one another via renaming. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_enable_memcard1.Help
data.value: Emulate a second memory card in the right memory card slot. Note: Some games require this option to be disabled for correct operation (e.g. Codename Tenka). Note: Memory Card Slot 2 uses the Mednafen (.mcr) save format. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_shared_memory_cards.Help
data.value: Use shared memory cards instead of separate cards for each content. Note: if 'Memory Card Method' is set to 'Libretro', only memory card slot 2 will be affected. Restart required.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_memcard_left_index.Help
data.value: Memory card currently loaded in the left slot. This option will only work if Memory Card Method is set to Mednafen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_memcard_right_index.Help
data.value: Memory card currently loaded in the right slot. This option will only work if Memory Card Slot 2 is enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_line_render.Help
data.value: Some games (e.g. Doom, Hexen, Soul Blade, etc.) draw horizontal lines by stretching single-pixel-high triangles across the screen, which are rasterized as a row of pixels on original hardware. This hack detects these small triangles and converts them to quads as required, allowing them to be displayed properly on the hardware renderers and at upscaled internal resolutions. 'Aggressive' is required for some titles (e.g. Dark Forces, Duke Nukem) but may otherwise introduce graphical glitches. Leave at 'Default' if unsure.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_widescreen_hack.Label
data.value: Modify the game for a wider screen

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_widescreen_hack.Help
data.value: Render 3D content anamorphically and output the emulated framebuffer at a widescreen aspect ratio. Produces best results with fully 3D games. 2D elements will be horizontally stretched and may be misaligned.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_widescreen_hack_aspect_ratio.Label
data.value: Aspect ratio for the wider screen

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_widescreen_hack_aspect_ratio.Help
data.value: Choose the aspect ratio used when modifying the game for a wider screen.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_spu_silent_voice.Help
data.value: Skip the per-sample processing of voices whose envelope has fully released. Audio output is identical; the optimization automatically disables itself while the SPU IRQ is in use. Saves roughly 5-10% of frame time. Disable for fully accurate SPU register state.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_cpu_dynarec.Help
data.value: Dynamically recompile CPU instructions to native instructions. Much faster than interpreter, but CPU timing is less accurate, and may have bugs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dynarec_invalidate.Help
data.value: Some games require 'Full' invalidation, some require 'DMA Only'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dynarec_op_cycles.Help
data.value: Cycles the dynarec charges per CPU instruction. '2' is faster, but the emulated CPU appears half-speed to games that pace themselves against it - set '1' for games whose CD streaming stalls or hangs under the dynarec (e.g. Parasite Eve 2). The '1' setting charges memory accesses two cycles and everything else one, close to the real CPU.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dynarec_eventcycles.Help
data.value: Max cycles run by CPU before a GPU/DMA/MDEC/Timer Update is checked, higher number will be faster, has much less impact on beetle interpreter than dynarec.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dynarec_spu_samples.Help
data.value: Max SPU samples to run before a SPU Update is checked, higher number will be faster, but will cause sound glitches in some games with anything other than 1.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dynarec_spgp_opt.Label
data.value: Dynarec SP GP Hit RAM Optimization

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_dynarec_spgp_opt.Help
data.value: Enabled will generate faster code, but potentially crash, by assuming sp and gp registers always point to ram, disabled is more widely compatible

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_compatibility_settings.Help
data.value: Apply compatibility settings per game and per setting. Disable to allow user-selected settings to override them.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_core_timing_fps.Help
data.value: Automatic Toggling allows the core to switch between progressive and interlaced rates.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_deinterlacer.Help
data.value: Weave joins both video fields in one frame. Still images retain full resolution. Bob reduces vertical resolution to make movement clearer. Bob (Offset) doubles the current field to fill the full image height. It shifts alternate fields by one line. This preserves the output resolution and smooth movement. FastMAD joins fields for still pixels and interpolates moving pixels vertically. It keeps full image height without comb-shaped artifacts during movement or the reduced resolution of Bob. When deinterlacing is disabled, the software renderer behaves like the Vulkan and OpenGL renderers. Every frame draws all VRAM lines before displaying the image. This removes comb-shaped artifacts in interlaced games. Some programs transfer data to VRAM while the image is being displayed. Some PAL demos do this with image buffers taller than 512 lines that wrap around. Other games, such as Pro Pinball, update moving sprites through CPU transfers to VRAM timed to the displayed field. These programs may show old image rows or duplicate sprite images when deinterlacing is disabled. Use Weave, Bob, Bob (Offset) or FastMAD for these programs.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_frame_duping.Help
data.value: Repeat the previous frame if the core has nothing new to display.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_pal_video_timing_override.Label
data.value: Override the timing of PAL video

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_pal_video_timing_override.Help
data.value: Due to different standards, PAL games often appear slowed down compared to the American or Japanese NTSC releases. This option can be used to override PAL timings in order to attempt to run these games with the NTSC framerate.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_aspect_ratio.Help
data.value: This setting is ignored when the Widescreen Mode Hack or Display Full VRAM options are enabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_crop_overscan.Help
data.value: Full native image or no borders.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_image_crop.Help
data.value: Reduce the width of the cropped image by the specified number of pixels.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_image_offset.Help
data.value: Offset horizontally to the right (positive) or left (negative) by the specified number of pixels. May be used to correct alignment issues. Only supported by the software renderer.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_image_offset_cycles.Help
data.value: Positive values move image to the right, negative values move image to the left. Only supported by the hardware renderers.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_initial_scanline.Help
data.value: First displayed scan line when running NTSC content. Values greater than zero will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the topmost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_last_scanline.Help
data.value: Last displayed scan line when running NTSC content. Values less than 239 will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the bottommost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_initial_scanline_pal.Help
data.value: First displayed scan line when running PAL content. Values greater than zero will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the topmost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.mednafen_psx_hw.beetle_psx_hw_last_scanline_pal.Help
data.value: Last displayed scan line when running PAL content. Values below 287 will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the bottommost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_region.Help
data.value: Specify which region the system is from. 'NTSC' is 60 Hz while 'PAL' is 50 Hz. 'Auto' will detect the region of the currently loaded content. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_bios.Help
data.value: Choose the BIOS to use. Automatic mode tries to load a BIOS file from the system folder. If no file is available, it emulates the BIOS instead. HLE mode always emulates the BIOS. An official BIOS file is recommended for better game compatibility.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_show_bios_bootlogo.Help
data.value: When using a custom BIOS file, enables the display of its file name in the OSD. Also specifies whether to show the BIOS logo when starting or selecting Reset. Warning: Enabling the logo may reduce game compatibility.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_memcard1.Help
data.value: How to emulate the memory card in slot 1. 'Libretro' passes the card data to the frontend (usually saved as .srm). 'Game Code' saves it to a file named based on the serial, such as SCUS-00001_1.mcd, for compatibility with some other emulators.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_memcard2.Help
data.value: Same as above, but card in slot 2.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_cd_readahead.Help
data.value: Reads the specified amount of sectors ahead of time to try to avoid later stalls. Affects both physical CD-ROM and CD images. 333000 will try to read the complete disk (requires an additional 750MB of RAM).

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_drc.Help
data.value: Dynamically recompile PSX CPU instructions to native instructions. Much faster than using an interpreter, but may be less accurate on some platforms.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_psxclock.Help
data.value: Overclock or under-clock the PSX CPU. Should be much less than 100 (something like 57) due to some real hardware slowdowns not being emulated. Usually should be left at 'Auto', else glitches or hangs are likely.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_dithering.Help
data.value: Enable emulation of the dithering technique used by the PSX to smooth out color banding artifacts. "Force" enables it even if the game turns it off. Increases performance requirements.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_gpu_thread_rendering.Help
data.value: When enabled, runs GPU commands in a secondary thread. 'Auto' enables it if at least 2 CPU cores are detected.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_frameskip_type.Help
data.value: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_frameskip_threshold.Help
data.value: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_frameskip_interval.Help
data.value: Specify the maximum number of frames that can be skipped before a new frame is rendered.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_display_fps_v2.Help
data.value: Show the internal frame rate at which the emulated system is rendering content. Note: Requires on-screen notifications to be enabled in the libretro frontend.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_display_info.Help
data.value: Shows things like unsafe hack options that are enabled and the BIOS name that is booting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_fractional_framerate.Help
data.value: Instead of the exact 50 or 60 (maximum) fps for PAL/NTSC the real console runs closer to something like 49.75 and 59.81fps (varies slightly between hw versions). PCSX-ReARMed uses the former "round" framerates to better match modern displays, however that may cause audio/video desync in games like DDR and Spyro 2 (intro). With this option you can try to use fractional framerates.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_alt_flip.Help
data.value: Some games make changes to the framebuffer while it's being sent to the display, which is currently not emulated. However this option allows to choose if the emulator takes the video frame before the emulated PSX active display period ('Early') or after ('Late'). Normally this should be left at 'Auto'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_rgb32_output.Help
data.value: Improves color depth for true color modes (most FMVs and occasional title screens). Causes higher CPU usage due to double memory bandwidth requirement, even in 15bpp modes. Takes effect on game reload only (libretro limitation).

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_scale_hires.Help
data.value: When enabled, games that run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) will be downscaled to 320x240 by skipping lines and/or columns. May be useful on some devices with native 240p display resolutions that lack efficient hardware scaling.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_gpu_slow_llists.Help
data.value: Slower but more accurate GPU linked list processing. Needed by only a few games like Vampire Hunter D. Should be autodetected in most cases.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_show_overscan.Help
data.value: The PSX can display graphics way into the horizontal borders, even if most screens would crop it. This option tries to display all such graphics. Note that this may result in unusual resolutions that your device might not handle well. The 'Hack' option is intended for the widescreen hacks.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_screen_centering.Help
data.value: The PSX has a feature allowing it to shift the image position on screen. Some (mostly PAL) games used this feature in a strange way making the image miscentered and causing uneven borders to appear. With 'Auto' the emulator tries to correct this miscentering automatically. 'Game-controlled' uses the settings supplied by the game. 'Manual' allows to override those values with the settings below.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_screen_centering_x.Help
data.value: X offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_screen_centering_y.Help
data.value: Y offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_screen_centering_h_adj.Help
data.value: Height adjustment. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_neon_interlace_enable_v2.Help
data.value: When enabled, games using 480i or 512i video modes produce an interlaced image. This image displays correctly on CRT televisions, but can show unwanted artifacts on modern screens. When disabled, the image is always progressive. Some games may display incorrectly when this option is disabled.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_neon_enhancement_enable.Help
data.value: Render games that do not already run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) at twice the native internal resolution. Improves the fidelity of 3D models at the expense of increased performance requirements. 2D elements are generally unaffected by this setting.

data.name: Emulation.Option.pcsx_rearmed.pcsx_rearmed_neon_enhancement_no_main.Help
data.value: Improve speed when the increased resolution modification is enabled. This reduces game compatibility and can cause graphics errors.
